posts.name: 39-world-human-breath-co2
posts.caption:
Human bodies release about 2 billion tonnes of CO2 a year just by staying alive, a new Lancet Planetary Health study estimates 🫁

The total rose 74% from 1985 to 2015, mostly because there are more of us. The authors say this carbon comes from food that plants recently pulled from the air, so it is not like fossil fuel emissions. The point is better carbon accounting for cities, not breathing or eating less.

Source: Gonzalez, Speakman et al. (University of Bath), “Accounting for global carbon dioxide production from human metabolism between 1985 and 2015: a modelling study”, The Lancet Planetary Health, 2026.
